public_sources.title: SkillGen: Verified Inference-Time Agent Skill Synthesis
observations: The paper explicitly models skills as interventions and compares outcomes on the same instances with and without the skill, counting both repairs and regressions.
ScienceWorld uses a 150-instance construction split and a 100-instance held-out test split in the controlled protocol.
Across the eight reported base agents, ScienceWorld held-out accuracy improves for every agent; the table reports deltas of +16, +3, +10, +3, +8, +25, +3, and +13 percentage points respectively.
The construction-time gate accepts a candidate only when verification net gain clears its threshold and persists failed candidates as deprecated no-op interventions for downstream evaluation.

The paper reports 2.2M construction tokens for ScienceWorld and states all experiments were orchestrated locally but model inference was executed through hosted LLM APIs routed through OpenRouter; the mean construction budget across benchmarks is reported as approximately USD 8.2 per generated skill.
public_sources.scope: This is strong same-instance paired intervention evidence and a useful evidence-packaging pattern, but its live construction/verification route fails the Phase-1 zero-optional-quota and zero-incremental-cost acceptance constraints.

public_sources.revision_chronology: current public main commit 2026-05-08T17:36:46Z, preceding arXiv v1 submission by about 25h47m; Git timestamp is chronology metadata, not evaluated-run execution time
observations: The current public repository includes exact ScienceWorld train/test JSON blobs at train sha ef71b989da4b3c68dc03723289350994f06c556a and test sha cfcf7ef2644c13c66c5475540942585c9828dde6.

effectiveness.py builds/reuses one baseline cache keyed by instance_id, executes the candidate skill on the same target-failure plus boundary-success instances, then records paired per-instance baseline_success, skill_success, outputs, repair/regression counts, net gain, baseline/skill trajectory JSONL paths, and a JSON summary.
artifacts.py serializes trajectories with explicit inference_model and judge_model fields, and provides checkpoint/resume files checkpoint_trajectories.jsonl plus checkpoint.json.

router.py is an optional per-instance gate that takes one task plus one fixed candidate skill and returns apply/skip; skipped instances clone the baseline trajectory. However router.enabled is false in the current default config and the arXiv paper text inspected contains no router mechanism, so router behavior is not attributed to the reported ScienceWorld results.
config.yaml routes model calls through hosted providers and uses OpenAI/OpenRouter models; it therefore does not provide a quota-zero live path.
public_sources.scope: The paired verification implementation is close to a same-candidate receiver-effect comparison at the instance level and provides a concrete auditable artifact schema. It is not a Phase-1 accepted execution mechanism because candidate generation and verification require hosted model calls; the optional router is code-level evidence only, not paper-result evidence.

findings.summary: SpeedRunner current code gives an exact raw-artifact target for ScienceWorld task 3: task-family evaluation writes under <run_dir>/dev/task_id_3/dev_epoch_<n>.jsonl, while the root explicitly ignores /runs/. Official Releases are empty and the inspected main Actions run has no artifacts, so the missing Figure-12 raw bundle is now localized to a runtime-output/export gap rather than an unspecified repository search gap.

MemCompiler's official GitHub Actions artifact surface is pages-only. Three github-pages artifacts are identifiable by size and digest but expired after one day; the complete webpage tree contains only static docs/images and no memory DB/run manifest. This inspected official artifact surface therefore cannot bind Table-3 ScienceWorld evaluated memory state.

SkillGen supplies a stronger public evidence-packaging pattern than the previously inspected memory systems: the paper defines same-instance with/without-skill verification, and current code serializes paired baseline/skill trajectories plus per-instance outcomes and model metadata. ScienceWorld improves for all eight reported agents, but the live construction/verification route explicitly uses hosted APIs and nonzero token cost, so it is scientific evidence and a packaging blueprint, not a Phase-1 zero-quota/zero-cost accepted route.

SkillGen's optional current router is a true receiver-side apply/skip gate over one fixed skill and one task, with fail-safe skip-on-error semantics, but router.enabled=false by default and the inspected arXiv paper contains no router description. It must not be retroactively used to explain the published ScienceWorld gains without a run/source binding.

skillgen_live_route_rejection_reasons: Nonzero reported construction token budget and monetary cost
No static published result bundle located that lets scheduled Chat reproduce the paired model outcomes without executing the model calls

uncertainties: No claim is made that SpeedRunner Figure-12 raw runs do not exist outside the inspected official GitHub release/action/tree surfaces.
